place.source_title: Row of storefronts with a barber shop (Vermilion)

brief: A row of one- and two-storey clapboard shops with striped awnings and bunting, a barber pole and a bench on the walk. Two photos (the barber shop is the middle front). Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: a row of small frame shopfronts (Vermilion OH, 1890s): one-storey false fronts painted in different pastels with bracketed cornices, red-and-white striped awnings, a barber pole, a brick shop with a shake mansard; benches and planters

why.note: varied colours, one height and rhythm: the row holds together
